method: difference of each epoch from the inverse-variance mean of all epochs (static sky cancels); Gaussian matched filter with a noise model from the weight maps plus a bright-star systematic; shift-and-stack over trial velocities using all epochs at once; local fits of a moving-source model and a fixed variable-source model (template subtraction built into both); Gaia DR3 proper motions label known movers; a motion common to bright stars is an alignment residual and is dropped; one threshold set for every field. Not a detection claim: candidates are for a person to inspect.
validation: Finds objects that move at least about 10 arcsec (about the width of a star image) over the time covered; slower motion is mostly missed.
In a sparse field an object at S/N 12 per pass moving 15 arcsec was recovered in 18 of 18 injections; in a crowded field in 8 of 18.

Grade A: seen in two independent wavelength ranges, or in three passes on a straight line, or a known moving star. Grade B: one wavelength range only; very cold objects look like this, and so do most false alarms.
